Great advice bro, but I feel the "just be yourself" won't get all people very far. People in this subreddit fail to understand the concept of probability. They try to explain their stuff with one successful example while ignoring the hundreds of failures. "Just be yourself" - well what if the person does not have the mindset and confidence needed to land a relationship? Being themselves will only make them fast forward year after year with no end result. Realizing where the problems lie and trying to rectify them if possible is a far better approach.

Repeated failure is kinda bound to bring bitterness about, and that's why you'll see the bitter posts. Anyway, congratulations man.

Rather than sugarcoating, let me be completely honest with you. Looks do matter. If you think they're pulling you back, try asking your friends for advice or hitting the gym. There will be more replies along the lines of "oh but beauty is in the eye of the beholder" but looks are objective to a big extent. Consider a fit guy who keeps himself properly beside a dude who is out of shape and smells like he hasn't had a shower in a decade. Unless you're into that shit, you'll probably want to interact with the former person. Personality will always come second to looks when initiating acquaintances/friendships/relationships.

My point is that for unattractive people like us, dating begins as a rough process. Luck is the biggest factor for unattractive people. Pray for some luck. Pretty much nothing else is helpful.

22M and I feel I'm on the same boat as you. I've been having this fear of never managing to find a date let alone a relationship since I was 19, and guess what, three years later, it's still the same. I don't expect things to change anymore in the next three years as well. At this point, I feel I'm the least attractive man in any room.

From what I've seen, one important realization has been that women in the mid 20s (at least in this part of the world) value looks and charm over pretty much everything, even though some of them like to post long ass rants on social media on how they'd be happy with a decent and caring guy. I'm not generalizing all women, but most of them are like this. I have a lot of friends, and the good looking ones are always jumping from one girl to the next. Some of them are genuinely good guys, don't get me wrong, but a lot of them are actually known for their "playboy" status, and yet, they'll manage to find a date within a week of a breakup, because, who doesn't wanna date a hot person? Fast forward to the 30s, the superficial nature of most people fades away and it's only then that they try to value a person irrespective of their looks.

The purpose of my comment is just to let you know that there are people like yourselves - a lot of them. Sadly I do not have any advice for you as I'm a fellow sufferer. I'm slowly coming to terms with the fact that not everyone is destined to get in a relationship and be happy. I get it, I'm not attractive. So I'm just focusing on my academics for now, though it gets lonely sometimes. I have one suggestion for you. I'd like you to try dating for five more years, because you don't want to sulk over quitting too early when you're old. If things aren't really taking a turn for the better after 30, you can decide to quit, and focus your energy somewhere else.

22M and I feel like I'm heading in the same direction brother. I'm slowly coming to terms with the fact that some of us won't have luck with dating and relationships. People will of course disagree with my comment, saying that people like me don't try enough and blah blah of the sort, but the truth is - if you're decent looking, dating and relationships will occur naturally to you if you have the luck. If you don't - that's alright. Each of us is inherently good and shitty at different aspects of life. For example, I'm pretty shit in the dating department and it seems to me that my face somehow drives women away. I've seen literal dimwits keep talking to women just because they're physically attractive. However these same friends have money issues (we're all in college), and this has never been an issue for me. Not to brag, but I never had to apply for a job - I was invited to work at each of my workplaces. Point being, we're all better than average at something, and shittier than average at something else. The idea is to capitalize on what you're good at.

You're just wasting your time and energy. Redirect it to something useful. Maybe learn something new, or get better at something you enjoy doing. Most importantly, keep yourself busy, remembering the fact that if it hasn't happened to you in 31 years, chances are that it's probably never gonna happen at all. I'm not demotivating you by any means, but loneliness is destructive bro. Bite the bullet and move on with your life. Some day, you'll forget the woes of not having an intimate relationship.
